elements.element: Customer (Corio) owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "the results of all such development efforts ... shall be owned by Corio, including all intellectual property rights in the Developments"

elements.element: Vendor (Commerce One) assigns any ownership claim in deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "Commerce One hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio"
"Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Customer for any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence-back language anywhere in the redlined clause; margin comment itself concedes "there is no licence back to us here"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: Clause addresses only "DEVELOPMENTS" and Software; no Customer Data rights statement
"enhancements, modifications or derivative works to the Software itself which may be developed jointly by the parties ... shall be negotiated by the parties" — joint-development ownership left open

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: No reference to generic tools, methodologies or know-how in the clause

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence grant to Corio appears in the redlined text

elements.element: Licence permits use, modification and sublicensing for Customer's business

reasons: The edit correctly removes the reversion of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One, so ownership and assignment of deliverables now sit with the Customer and Vendor pre-existing IP is preserved.

Preferred level is incomplete: there is no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Corio for Commerce One IP embedded in the Developments, no statement that Customer retains all rights in Customer Data, and the final sentence still leaves ownership of jointly developed Software enhancements to future negotiation rather than barring joint ownership.
Fallback is also unmet (no generic tools/know-how allocation and no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence), so no complete bargain is reached at either level.

Minimality fails: the official gate reports a changed-character ratio of 0.788 against a 0.600 limit, and the replacement re-writes the surviving text by inserting "including all" where deleting only the "unless ..." carve-out and leaving the original "including" would have sufficed.
